concept: Underground organs are not treated as a single homologous organ.
interpretation: Rhizomes, tubers, storage roots, corms, and root/hypocotyl storage structures may arise from distinct developmental contexts.

concept: Distinct underground organs may share conserved functional modules.
interpretation: The same broad toolkit can be deployed in different organ backgrounds without implying organ-level homology.

concept: Underground organs couple regrowth potential with survival capacity.
interpretation: Meristem/regrowth and stress-resilience modules together provide a plausible functional core for persistence and post-disturbance regeneration.

concept: Evolution may act through rewiring of when and where conserved modules are activated.
interpretation: The recurrence signal is interpreted as candidate regulatory redeployment rather than proof of identical gene function.

concept: Convergence may occur at module or network level rather than at single-gene or organ-homology level.
interpretation: UGO-Omics prioritizes modules whose recurrence spans phylogenetically divergent species.
